title: made the word study extension
summary: Adds a new built-in **Word Study** extension. After you install it, selecting one or more verses shows a **Word Study** button in the verse toolbar. It opens a side pane listing the original Hebrew or Greek words of each verse, with transliteration, English gloss, Strong's number and grammar. Tapping a word opens its lexicon entry (definition, senses, tappable verse references and a CC BY attribution). The chapter interlinear view and the concordance from issue 2138 are not part of this PR.

links.label: Issue 2140: extension package and cached data

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. One section also needs a phone (iPhone Safari or Android Chrome); if you don't have one, a computer browser window made as narrow as it goes (then reloaded) works too. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Start clean and sign in
setup.body: Use a private/incognito window, so nothing is left over from earlier visits. Sign in with your email address (you'll be sent a code, so use an inbox you can check). Installing extensions needs an account.

setup.title: Use a light theme and an English Bible to start
setup.body: The tests assume the app's light theme and an English translation (any one) unless they say otherwise. To select a verse, click (or tap) its verse number or text; the verse gets highlighted and the verse toolbar appears with buttons like **Copy**, **Compare** and **Share**.

tests.title: Word Study can be installed from the extensions list
tests.why: The extension isn't installed for anyone by default (issue 2140 asks for that until the design is reviewed), so this is how every tester reaches it.
steps: Open the app's menu and go to **Extensions**.
Find **Word Study** (it's under **Available**; the search box helps).
Open it and choose **Install**.
expected: Before installing, **Word Study** is listed under **Available**, not **Installed**, with the description "See the original Hebrew and Greek words behind the verses you select, with Strong's numbers, grammar and lexicon definitions."
After installing, it moves under **Installed**.

tests.title: The Word Study button only shows while a verse is selected
steps: Go to **John 1**.
Select verse 1.
Look at the verse toolbar.
Deselect the verse (choose **Cancel** in the toolbar, or click the verse again).
expected: With the verse selected, the toolbar has a **Word Study** button (a translate icon), between **Compare** and **Share**.
With nothing selected, no Word Study button is shown anywhere.

tests.title: A Greek verse shows one row per original word
steps: Go to **John 1** and select verse 1.
Choose **Word Study** in the verse toolbar.
expected: A pane opens at the side with the title **Word Study** and the reference **John 1:1**. While it loads you may briefly see grey placeholder lines.

Under a **John 1:1** heading there is one row per Greek word. Each row shows the Greek word, how to pronounce it (for example **Logos**), a short English meaning (for example **Word**), a Strong's number (for example **G3056**) and a short grammar code (for example **N-NMS**).
At the bottom: "Interlinear data: Berean Standard Bible (public domain)".

tests.title: The grammar code can be expanded into plain words
tests.before: The Word Study pane is open on John 1:1.
steps: On a computer, hover the mouse over a grammar code such as **N-NMS** and wait a moment.
Click (or tap) the grammar code.
Click it again.
expected: Hovering shows a tooltip with the grammar in words, such as "Noun - Nominative Masculine Singular".
Clicking shows that same text in words under the row, and the arrow next to the code flips. Clicking again hides it.
Someone who doesn't know the codes could understand the expanded text.

tests.title: Words can be listed in original or English order
tests.why: Issue 2141 asks for this toggle because Hebrew word order is very different from English.
steps: Go to **Genesis 1**, select verse 1 and choose **Word Study**.
Note the order of the English meanings down the rows.
At the top of the pane, choose **English order**.
Choose **Original order** again.
expected: At the top of the pane are two buttons, **Original order** and **English order**, with **Original order** selected to start.

In original order the meanings read roughly "In the beginning / created / God / … / the heavens / and / the earth" (Hebrew order). In English order they read in the order of the English sentence ("In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth").
Switching back restores the first order.

tests.title: Hebrew words read right to left with their vowel marks
tests.before: The Word Study pane is open on Genesis 1:1.
steps: Look closely at the Hebrew words in each row.
expected: Each Hebrew word is written right to left and lines up on the right-hand side of its space, with its small dots and marks (vowel points and accents) above and below the letters, not as empty boxes or separate symbols.

tests.title: Several selected verses each get their own heading
steps: Close the Word Study pane (its close button in the pane header).
Go to **John 1** and select verses 1, 2 and 3.
Choose **Word Study**.
expected: The pane title shows **John 1:1–3**.
The pane lists the words of each verse under its own heading: **John 1:1**, **John 1:2**, **John 1:3**, in that order.

tests.title: The pane keeps its label when you move to another chapter
tests.why: Issue 2141: the pane must never show old words without saying which verse they belong to.
tests.before: The Word Study pane is open on John 1:1–3 (previous test).
steps: Without closing the pane, move the reader to **John 2** (next chapter).
expected: The pane still says **John 1:1–3** in its title and headings, and still shows those verses' words. It does not show John 1's words under a John 2 heading.

tests.title: Books the word data doesn't cover show a clear message
tests.why: The interlinear data doesn't include the deuterocanonical books (Tobit, Judith, 1–2 Maccabees and others).
tests.before: You need a translation that includes Tobit. In the translation picker, look for one with "Apocrypha", "Catholic" or "Deuterocanon" in its name. If you can't find one, mark this test **Skip** and say so.
steps: Switch to that translation and go to **Tobit 1**.
Select verse 1 and choose **Word Study**.
expected: Under the **Tobit 1:1** heading the pane says "Word study isn't available for this book yet." No error, no endless loading.

tests.title: A verse numbered differently from the data shows a clear message
tests.why: Some translations number verses differently. For example, German Bibles end Malachi at chapter 3 with verses 19–24, which English Bibles call chapter 4.
tests.before: You need a translation whose Malachi chapter 3 has 24 verses, such as a German Luther Bible. If you can't find one, mark this test **Skip** and say so.
steps: Switch to that translation and go to **Malachi 3**.
Select verse 20 and choose **Word Study**.
expected: The pane says "Word study isn't available for this verse." It doesn't show some other verse's words.

tests.title: Tapping a word opens its lexicon entry
steps: Switch back to an English translation. Go to **John 1**, select verse 1 and choose **Word Study**.
Tap the row for **Logos** (Word, **G3056**).
expected: The pane title changes to **Lexicon**, and a back arrow appears at the start of the pane header.
The card shows the Greek word (λόγος), its pronunciation, its part of speech, a short meaning and **G3056**, then a longer definition below.

The definition is easy to read: paragraphs, and numbered or lettered points shown as an indented list. There are no stray double underscores (`__`) or raw codes like `
`.
At the bottom: "Definitions: STEPBible.org / Tyndale House, Cambridge, CC BY 4.0", where both the source name and **CC BY 4.0** are links.

tests.title: Back returns to the word list where you left it
tests.before: The lexicon card for G3056 is open (previous test).
steps: Press the back arrow in the pane header.
expected: The word list for John 1:1 comes back straight away (no reloading), at the same scroll position, and the title shows **Word Study** and **John 1:1** again.

tests.title: A word with several senses shows all of them
tests.why: Many Hebrew entries have several senses (issue 2142 uses H0430 as the example).
steps: Go to **Genesis 1**, select verse 1 and choose **Word Study**.
Tap the row whose meaning is **God** (Strong's **H0430**).
expected: The card shows more than one sense, each with its own Hebrew word, pronunciation, meaning, part of speech and its own id (such as **H0430G**, **H0430H**).
If the card has a **Sense referred to** heading, the sense under it is the one matching this word, and the rest are under **Other senses**.

tests.title: Verse references in a definition take you to that verse
steps: Open the lexicon card for **Logos** (G3056) from John 1:1 again.
Find a verse reference in the definition (written like `Mat.8:8` or `Jhn.2:22`) that looks like a link, and tap it.
expected: References the app understands are shown as links. Tapping one moves the reader to that verse (on a computer, the pane stays open beside it).
Nothing that looks like a link leads nowhere or shows an error. References the app can't understand are plain text.

tests.title: Strong's numbers in a definition open that entry
steps: In any lexicon card, look for a Strong's number written inside the definition text (such as `H3068G` or `G1722`). The Genesis 1:1 entries for **God** (H0430) or **LORD** words are good places to look.
Tap it.
Press the back arrow twice.
expected: Tapping it opens that entry's card.
The first back press returns to the card you came from; the second returns to the word list.

tests.title: A word with no Strong's number can't be tapped
tests.why: Issue 2141: such words still show, but have no lexicon entry. Only a few words lack a number, so you may need to look around.
steps: Open Word Study on a few verses and look for a row with no Strong's number at the end (try selecting a whole chapter's worth of verses, for example **Genesis 1:1–10**).
If you find one, hover over it and tap it.
expected: The row is shown with its word, pronunciation and grammar, just without a Strong's number.
Hovering says "This word has no Strong's number, so it has no lexicon entry." Tapping it does nothing.
If you couldn't find such a row, mark the test **Skip** and say so.

tests.title: No connection shows an error with Retry, and Retry recovers
tests.before: Close the Word Study pane. Go to **Psalm 23** while still online and wait for the text to show.
steps: Turn off your Wi-Fi (or turn on airplane mode).
Select **Psalm 23:1** and choose **Word Study**.
Turn Wi-Fi back on and wait a few seconds.
Choose **Retry** in the pane.
expected: While offline the pane says "Couldn't load the original words. Check your connection and try again." with a **Retry** button. It doesn't stay on loading placeholders forever.
After Retry, the Hebrew words of Psalm 23:1 appear.

tests.title: Words already looked at still show offline
tests.why: Issue 2140: word data is saved on the device so a chapter you've opened works without a connection.
steps: Close the pane and turn Wi-Fi off again.
Select **Psalm 23:2** and choose **Word Study**.
Tap a word you haven't opened before.
Turn Wi-Fi back on.
expected: The words of Psalm 23:2 show even though you're offline (the whole chapter was saved when you opened verse 1).
The lexicon card for a word not opened before says "Couldn't load this definition. Check your connection and try again." with a **Retry** button, which works once you're back online.

tests.title: The pane works at phone width
steps: On a phone (or a very narrow browser window), open the preview and go to **John 1**.
Select verse 1 and choose **Word Study**.
Tap a word, then tap a verse reference inside its definition.
expected: The pane fills the screen (like **Compare** does on a phone). Rows fit the width without text cut off or sideways scrolling, and the order buttons and grammar codes are easy to tap.
Tapping a verse reference closes the pane and shows the reader at that verse.

tests.title: The pane follows dark mode
steps: Switch the app to its dark theme.
Open Word Study on **Genesis 1:1**, then open a lexicon card.
expected: The pane and card use the dark theme's colors. All text, links, the order buttons and the Strong's numbers are easy to read; nothing is dark-on-dark or a white box.

sections.title: Uninstalling, and things that should not have changed

tests.title: Uninstall removes the button, and reinstalling brings it back
tests.why: Issue 2140 asks that the extension uninstalls cleanly and reinstalls in the same session.
steps: With the Word Study pane open, go to the app's menu › **Extensions**, open **Word Study** and uninstall it.
Go back to the reader and select a verse.
Without reloading the page, install **Word Study** again, select a verse and choose **Word Study**.
expected: After uninstalling, the Word Study pane closes and the verse toolbar no longer has a Word Study button.
After reinstalling, the button is back and the pane opens with the verse's words as before.

tests.title: Cross-references and Compare still work
tests.why: The PR changes how the app loads the dataset files that the References extension and Discover also use.
steps: In **Extensions**, install **References** if it isn't installed.
Go to **John 3** and open the cross-references for verse 16 the way you normally would (for example by tapping its cross-reference count).
Select a verse and choose **Compare**.
expected: Cross-references for John 3:16 load as before (a list of related verses, not an error or endless loading).
Compare opens and shows the verse in other translations as before.

notCovered: The chapter interlinear reading view (issue 2143) and the list of every verse that uses a word (issue 2144). Neither is part of this PR.
That saved word data expires after 30 days and "not found" answers after a day. That's covered by automated tests; it can't be checked by hand in a reasonable time.
Translations of the new text into other languages. Only English is added, on purpose; other languages are left for translators.
